# Row keep fitting at the page edge

Original manually authored XML generated by `tools/row_keep_fitting_fixture.py`.
No template artwork or third-party engine code is included. Arial is required.
Native PDFs were exported using the reference application and
`tools/export-reference.ps1`. JSON hashes bind the exact source and PDF.
Marker page numbers come from PDF text extraction, independently of the engine.

The base pair has a 488.2pt spacer, then a fixed-width two-row table. The first
row's right cell has paragraphs of 8, 2 and 5 lines, exact 14pt line spacing,
and 12pt after-spacing. Only the first left-cell paragraph's keepNext differs.
Without it, the reference application keeps the first row on page 1; with it, it moves it to page 2.

The three next-* controls vary only the following row's line height. A 1pt
line lets both rows stay on page 1; 4pt and 40pt lines move the kept row to page 2.
Together with the older first-cell-keep two-row controls, this distinguishes
reserving the following row's initial content from keeping its full height.
The previous implementation reserved nothing for an interior kept row.
The correction uses the following row's existing minimum-content calculation
when it terminates the keep chain, preserving ordinary paragraph/table-boundary
keeps and the existing first-cell row-split behavior.

ECMA-376 Part 1 17.3.1.15 defines paragraph keepNext. Applying the first physical
cell's first paragraph keep to the row and the following row's initial content
is observed native compatibility beyond the paragraph-level description. Vertical
merge groups and repeated headers retain their existing separate pagination
paths; these controls do not certify every combination with those features.

All five native marker comparisons pass. Browser workflows cover editable
opening, insertion, undo and reopening; a unit regression toggles the first-cell
keep, verifies changed pagination, checks unrelated package parts and reopening,
and requires exact package restoration on undo. The original #23 Arial diagnostic
now places its instructions and later rule on the same pages as the reference application. Missing
original fonts and cached field updates remain separate fidelity issues.
